rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine). Model uses affine=True by default, initializing weight=ones(64) and bias=zeros(64), both defined tensors. C++ dispatch checks (weight.defined() && bias.defined()) which is always true, so instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine is called instead. The mutated kernel is dead code.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies the reduction condition in instance_norm_forward_kernel, but this kernel is only called when either weight or bias is undefined. Since the model uses affine=True by default, both weight and bias are always initialized as defined Parameter tensors. The C++ dispatch logic always routes to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, leaving the mutated non-affine kernel unreachable. No input tensor value can change this dispatch decision since it depends solely on model configuration, not input data.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed configuration. To kill it, one would need to either: (1) set affine=False when constructing InstanceNorm2dCustom, or (2) pass undefined weight/bias tensors. Both require configuration changes, not value changes to the input tensor.
rounds.recommendations: When testing GPU kernels with multiple code paths (e.g., affine vs non-affine), ensure mutation testing exercises ALL paths. Create test fixtures with different model configurations, not just different input values, to achieve full code coverage of conditional kernel dispatches.
